newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Germany stands out against film guarantee fund.
newsitem.headline: Germany stands out against film guarantee fund.

text.p: Germany remains the main opponent of a European Commission plan to launch a guarantee fund to help the European Union's film industry, industry sources said on Thursday.
The Netherlands and Britain also maintained reservations on COM (95) 536 when the Council's working group discussed it last week, they said.
The plan for the fund should be discussed at the December 16 meeting of the Culture Council. The plan, as a matter involving money, would require unanimous approval by the Council.

The Commission is trying to win round the scepical member states by pointing to the results of a European Investment Fund study which demonstrated that a fund would survive on an initial EU contribution of 90 million Ecus for 17 years without a fresh injection of funds.
The study was carried out at the request of Britain, which wanted the feasibility and impact of such a fund spelled out.
The study showed that 17 years would give time enough to set up a guarantee fund as a legal entity.
Germany has expressed opposition to the fund on the grounds that culture is a national rather than a European issue.
